newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore authority says three phone bids received.
newsitem.headline: Singapore authority says three phone bids received.

text.p: The Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS) said it had received three pre-qualification bids to offer new fixed-wire telephone services in Singapore by the close of the tender on Saturday.
Submissions were made by a consortium comprising Cable and Wireless Plc and its unit Hong Kong Telecommunications, Keppel Telecoms and newspaper publisher Singapore Press Holdings Ltd.
The second group submitting a bid comprised British Telecommunications Plc, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and state-run Singapore Power and ST Telecommunications Pte Ltd.
Marine-based conglomerate SembCorp Ltd, state-owned railway company Singapore MRT Ltd and WorldCom Inc submitted the third bid on Friday.
A list of pre-qualified tenderers will be announced by September 1997, the TAS said in a statement.

The qualifying groups will then be given five months to prepare their main tender submissions with detailed technical and commercial proposals on how they intend to roll out and provide services in Singapore.

The TAS said it expected to announce the successful licensee by mid-1998, leaving at least 20 months lead time to build, roll out and test the network before the launch of commercial services from April 1, 2000.
